summary: Object tables are read-only tables that store metadata for unstructured data in Cloud Storage so it can be analyzed with BigQuery capabilities; Object tables are read-only BigQuery tables that store metadata for unstructured Cloud Storage objects.
extended_definition: Object tables are read-only tables that store metadata for unstructured data in Cloud Storage so it can be analyzed with BigQuery capabilities; Object tables are read-only BigQuery tables that store metadata for unstructured Cloud Storage objects.

supporting_pages.title: "Discover and catalog Cloud Storage data \_|\_ BigQuery \_|\_ Google Cloud\
evidence_snippets: The discovery scan supports the following compression formats: Structured and semi-structured data Internal compression for the following formats: Compression File extension sample Supported format gzip .gz.parquet Parquet lz4 .lz4.parquet Parquet Snappy .snappy.parquet Parquet, ORC, Avro lzo .lzo.parquet Parquet, ORC External compression for JSON and CSV files: gzip bzip2 Unstructured data For object tables, compression is managed primarily through Cloud Storage object metadata , rather than BigQuery internal settings.
For example, gs://images/group1 must only contain GIF images, and gs://images/group2 must only contain JPEG images for the discovery scan to detect and register two BigLake object tables.
As part of the discovery scan, automatic discovery creates BigLake or external tables for structured data and object tables for unstructured data.

supporting_pages.title: Create and use tables \_|\_ BigQuery \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: Create a multimodal table You can create a table with one or more ObjectRef columns in order to store metadata about unstructured data that is related to the other structured data in the table.
The unstructured data itself is stored in Cloud Storage, and is made available in BigQuery by using an object table .

supporting_pages.title: "Introduction to BigLake external tables \_|\_ BigQuery \_|\_ Google Cloud\
evidence_snippets: Cache-enabled tables with materialized views You can use materialized views over BigLake metadata cache-enabled tables to improve performance and efficiency when querying structured data stored in Cloud Storage or Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3).
As a result, metadata caching-enabled queries read data corresponding to the specific cached object version, even if newer versions become live in Cloud Storage.

To find information about metadata refresh jobs, query the INFORMATION SCHEMA.JOBS view , as shown in the following example: SELECT FROM region-us.INFORMATION SCHEMA.JOBS BY PROJECT WHERE job id LIKE '%metadata cache refresh%' AND creation time > TIMESTAMP SUB ( CURRENT TIMESTAMP (), INTERVAL 6 HOUR ) ORDER BY start time DESC LIMIT 10 ; For Cloud Storage BigLake tables that are based on Parquet files, table statistics are collected during the metadata cache refresh and used to improve query plans.
